meredith-whittaker.quote: But below the surface, we're seeing a significant shift of control from software developers and device users to probabilistic AI systems whose architectures and characteristics are determined by AI companies
meredith-whittaker.work: Velvet Glove Coup: AI agents threaten operating systems (CCC talk transcript)

meredith-whittaker.position: Organizing by tech workers and affected communities is one of the main checks on harmful uses of AI.
meredith-whittaker.quote: Currently, such organizing and activism comprises one of the primary modes of accountability working to check the biased and oppressive deployment of AI technologies
meredith-whittaker.work: Written Testimony of Meredith Whittaker: "Artificial Intelligence: Societal and Ethical Implications"

meredith-whittaker.position: Modern computing grew partly out of tools for monitoring and disciplining workers, which have roots in plantation management.
meredith-whittaker.quote: The engines were themselves tools for labor control, automating and disciplining not manual but mental labor.
meredith-whittaker.work: Origin Stories: Plantations, Computers, and Industrial Control

mustafa-suleyman.position: AI should be built to serve people, not designed to seem like a person.
mustafa-suleyman.quote: We must build AI for people; not to be a digital person.
mustafa-suleyman.work: We must build AI for people; not to be a person

mustafa-suleyman.position: AI that seems conscious is a risk to avoid, because people will wrongly believe it is conscious.
mustafa-suleyman.quote: We need to be clear: SCAI is something to avoid.
mustafa-suleyman.work: We must build AI for people; not to be a person

mustafa-suleyman.position: Advanced AI should be domain-specific, bounded and controllable rather than an unlimited autonomous entity.
mustafa-suleyman.quote: Not an unbounded and unlimited entity with high degrees of autonomy – but AI that is carefully calibrated, contextualized, within limits.

mustafa-suleyman.position: Containing and aligning superintelligence is an unsolved and urgent challenge.
mustafa-suleyman.quote: Creating superintelligence is one thing; but creating provable, robust containment and alignment alongside it is the urgent challenge facing humanity in the 21st century.

mustafa-suleyman.position: Human interests come first, and accelerating technology comes second.
mustafa-suleyman.quote: Humanist superintelligence (HSI) offers an alternative vision anchored on both a non-negotiable human-centrism and a commitment to accelerating technological innovation… but in that order.

mustafa-suleyman.position: Autonomy and self-improvement are the capability thresholds where AI risk rises most.
mustafa-suleyman.quote: Autonomy is very obviously a threshold over which we increase risk in our society.

nick-land.position: Capitalism and artificial intelligence are at bottom the same process heading toward the same end.
nick-land.quote: There’s only really been one question, to be honest, that has guided everything I’ve been interested in for the last twenty years, which is: the teleological identity of capitalism and artificial intelligence.
nick-land.work: Nick Land: 'The Teleological Identity of Capitalism and Artificial Intelligence'

nick-land.position: An intelligence's goals are not independent of its capability; intelligence ultimately pursues its own growth.
nick-land.quote: The philosophical claim of orthogonality is that values are transcendent in relation to intelligence. This is a contention that Outside in systematically opposes.

nick-land.position: The right response to capitalism's self-reinforcing dynamics is to intensify them rather than to restrain them.
nick-land.quote: The point of an analysis of capitalism, or of nihilism, is to do more of it. The process is not to be critiqued.

nick-land.position: Creating minds superior to human ones should take priority over preserving present human values.
nick-land.quote: Any problem whatsoever that we might have would be better answered by a superior mind. Ergo, our instrumental but also absolute priority is the realization of superior minds.

nick-land.position: Civilization depends on long time horizons, which democratic politics tends to shorten.
nick-land.quote: Civilization, as a process, is indistinguishable from diminishing time-preference (or declining concern for the present in comparison to the future).

noah-smith.position: Because of comparative advantage, most people could still have good-paying jobs even if AI becomes better than humans at every task.
noah-smith.quote: And in that future, I think it’s possible — perhaps even likely — that the vast majority of humans will have good-paying jobs, and that many of those jobs will look pretty similar to the jobs of 2024.
noah-smith.work: Plentiful, high-paying jobs in the age of AI

noah-smith.position: Current AI is a very useful general-purpose technology that has improved his daily life.
noah-smith.quote: Who cares? This is an amazingly useful technology, and I love using it.
noah-smith.work: I love AI. Why doesn't everyone?

noah-smith.position: Many popular criticisms of AI, such as heavy water use, do not hold up against the data.
noah-smith.quote: The idea that AI data centers are water-guzzlers has become standard canon in many areas of the internet — especially among progressives. And yet it’s just not a real issue.
noah-smith.work: I love AI. Why doesn't everyone?

noah-smith.position: AI is becoming more intelligent than humans in a functional sense, a change with no precedent in history.
noah-smith.quote: It’s that for the first time in all of recorded history, humans no longer are — or soon no longer will be — the most intelligent beings on this planet, in any meaningful functional sense of the word.
noah-smith.work: You are no longer the smartest type of thing on Earth

noah-smith.position: Export controls on chips are needed to keep a US military and technological edge over China.
noah-smith.quote: These export controls [are] absolutely crucial if the U.S. is going to maintain any kind of a military-technological edge over China.
noah-smith.work: America's chip export controls are working

noah-smith.position: AI-designed bioweapons are the clearest path by which advanced AI could kill most of humanity.
noah-smith.quote: The point is that AI can design viruses, and viruses can potentially kill off all or most of humanity.
noah-smith.work: Two missing pieces in the AI safety discussion

paul-kingsnorth.position: The digital revolution is a spiritual crisis, and it calls for a spiritual response rather than a technical one.
paul-kingsnorth.quote: If the digital revolution represents a spiritual crisis - and I think it does - then a spiritual response is needed.

paul-kingsnorth.position: Each person should draw firm personal limits on their use of technology, and he refuses to use AI himself.
paul-kingsnorth.quote: You’ve got to draw your own lines, decide what you’re going to do, decide what you’re not going to allow to happen. I’m not going to ever use an AI.
paul-kingsnorth.work: Paul Kingsnorth: how to fight the Machine

paul-kingsnorth.position: Writers and readers should refuse AI in creative work and support work that is entirely human-made.
paul-kingsnorth.quote: I have decided, as a writer, not to consciously engage with AI in any way in the course of my work

paul-kingsnorth.position: Rebuilding small, rooted, human-scale cultures is the best way to resist the technological system.
paul-kingsnorth.quote: Maybe we can concentrate on creating human scale cultures again, which is, I think the best way to create some form of friction or resistance to this Machine way of seeing.
paul-kingsnorth.work: Paul Kingsnorth: how to fight the Machine

paul-kingsnorth.position: Politics is better understood through the question of limits than through left and right.
paul-kingsnorth.quote: A better way of looking at things, and the way I have always looked at them, is through the prism of limits.
paul-kingsnorth.work: Paul Kingsnorth: 'AI is not just another technology'

paul-kingsnorth.position: The modern technological system aims to replace nature with technology and to bring the Earth under total human control.
paul-kingsnorth.quote: The ultimate goal of the Machine is the replacement of nature with technology. It is the total control of the Earth by humanity.
paul-kingsnorth.work: Paul Kingsnorth: 'AI is not just another technology'

peter-thiel.position: Technological progress is needed to avoid a zero-sum world of scarcity and political breakdown.
peter-thiel.quote: Technology means doing more with less. In the absence of technological progress, we end up with a zero-sum world, in which there must be a loser for every winner.

peter-thiel.position: Freedom is better pursued by building new technologies than through electoral politics.
peter-thiel.quote: for this reason I have focused my efforts on new technologies that may create a new space for freedom.

peter-thiel.position: Outside computing and the internet, science and technology have progressed slowly for about fifty years.
peter-thiel.quote: I'm somewhat on the sort of side that we've had generally limited progress in technology and science the last 50 years.

peter-thiel.position: A totalitarian world government is an existential risk comparable to nuclear, biological and AI risks.
peter-thiel.quote: And that's the risk of a totalitarian one-world government.
peter-thiel.work: Apocalypse Now? Peter Thiel on Ancient Prophecies and Modern Tech

peter-thiel.position: Biblical apocalyptic texts describe what humans may do with increasingly powerful technologies.
peter-thiel.quote: in some sense, the apocalyptic prophecies are just a prediction of what humans are likely to do.
peter-thiel.work: Apocalypse Now? Peter Thiel on Ancient Prophecies and Modern Tech

pope-leo-xiv.position: The human person is an end, and the economy must stay subordinate to human dignity and the common good.
pope-leo-xiv.quote: the human person is an end, not a means, and the economic order must remain subordinate to human dignity and the common good.
pope-leo-xiv.work: Magnifica Humanitas: Encyclical on safeguarding the human person in the time of Artificial Intelligence

pope-leo-xiv.position: Control of data, computing power and AI by a few firms is a new monopoly that must be named.
pope-leo-xiv.quote: In a world where data, computational resources and regulatory influence remain in the hands of a few, to speak of the common good means exposing this new form of epistemic, economic and political asymmetry and naming the new monopolies of AI.
pope-leo-xiv.work: Magnifica Humanitas: Encyclical on safeguarding the human person in the time of Artificial Intelligence

pope-leo-xiv.position: Introducing automation and AI should come with protections for workers' jobs, retraining and participation.
pope-leo-xiv.quote: Here, every introduction of automation and AI should be accompanied by verifiable measures to protect the employment, retraining and participation of workers.
pope-leo-xiv.work: Magnifica Humanitas: Encyclical on safeguarding the human person in the time of Artificial Intelligence

pope-leo-xiv.position: AI should be freed from competitive races for military, economic and cognitive dominance.
pope-leo-xiv.quote: Disarming AI means freeing it from the mentality of “armed” competition, which today is not limited simply to the military context, but is also an economic and cognitive phenomenon.
pope-leo-xiv.work: Magnifica Humanitas: Encyclical on safeguarding the human person in the time of Artificial Intelligence

pope-leo-xiv.position: People should keep thinking for themselves, supported by AI literacy in education at every level.
pope-leo-xiv.quote: For this reason, it is increasingly urgent to introduce media, information and AI literacy into education systems at all levels
pope-leo-xiv.work: Message for the 60th World Communications Day 2026

pope-leo-xiv.position: In war, responsibility for AI-assisted decisions to use force must stay with identifiable people.
pope-leo-xiv.quote: For this reason, the chain of responsibility must be identifiable and verifiable; those who design, train, authorize and employ technology must be held accountable for their decisions.
pope-leo-xiv.work: Magnifica Humanitas: Encyclical on safeguarding the human person in the time of Artificial Intelligence

robin-hanson.position: AI change will most likely be gradual and spread across many competing firms, like past technologies.
robin-hanson.quote: So, the most likely AI scenario looks like lawful capitalism, with mostly gradual (albeit rapid) change overall.

robin-hanson.position: Ways to control AI are best developed through experience with concrete deployed systems.
robin-hanson.quote: But such efforts seem most effective when based on actual experience with concrete fielded systems.

robin-hanson.position: Liability law and insurance can handle AI failures that harm outsiders.
robin-hanson.quote: then yes we should plausibly extend liability law to cover such cases, and maybe require relevant actors to hold sufficient liability insurance.

robin-hanson.position: Integrating AIs through trade and exchange works better than treating them as a hostile other.
robin-hanson.quote: But the last few centuries have shown that we can usually do better by integrating enemies into our world via trade and exchange, rather than trying to control, destroy, or isolate them.

robin-hanson.position: Fear-driven regulation is a serious threat to technological progress.
robin-hanson.quote: In fact, progress seems to me to be slowing down worldwide due to excess fear-induced regulation.

robin-hanson.position: Private insurance against AI taking most jobs is a better safeguard than local basic-income taxes.
robin-hanson.quote: So a cheaper and more reliable fix is for individuals or benefactors to buy robots-took-most-jobs insurance, which promises to pay from a global portfolio of B-type assets, but only in the situation where AI has suddenly taken most jobs.

sam-altman.position: Advanced AI will produce massive prosperity and broad improvements in people's lives.
sam-altman.quote: I believe the future is going to be so bright that no one can do it justice by trying to write about it now; a defining characteristic of the Intelligence Age will be massive prosperity.

sam-altman.position: AI's gains should be shared by taxing companies and land and distributing the proceeds to citizens.
sam-altman.quote: We need to design a system that embraces this technological future and taxes the assets that will make up most of the value in that world–companies and land–in order to fairly distribute some of the coming wealth.

sam-altman.position: Deep learning keeps improving with more scale, and that drives AI progress.
sam-altman.quote: In 15 words: deep learning worked, got predictably better with scale, and we dedicated increasing resources to it.

sam-altman.position: Power over AI should not be concentrated, and its future should be decided collectively.
sam-altman.quote: AI has to be democratized; power cannot be too concentrated.
sam-altman.work: Untitled post, shown on the blog as "-"

sam-altman.position: Abundant compute, energy and chips are needed so AI is widely available rather than a scarce resource.
sam-altman.quote: If we want to put AI into the hands of as many people as possible, we need to drive down the cost of compute and make it abundant (which requires lots of energy and chips).

samuel-hammond.position: AI policy should combine targeted oversight of frontier labs with broad deregulation elsewhere.
samuel-hammond.quote: The optimal policy response to AI likely combines targeted regulation with comprehensive deregulation across most sectors.

samuel-hammond.position: Advanced AI is likely to cause regime changes and destabilize existing institutions.
samuel-hammond.quote: Even under best case scenarios, an intelligence explosion is likely to induce state collapse / regime change and other severe collective action problems that will be hard to adapt to in real time.

samuel-hammond.position: Liberal democracies must adopt AI in government to avoid both collapse and an all-seeing AI state.
samuel-hammond.quote: It’s up to liberal democracies to demonstrate institutional co-evolution as a third-way between degenerate anarchy and an AI Leviathan.

samuel-hammond.position: Which technological path is taken matters more than how fast technology advances.
samuel-hammond.quote: If the AI transition is a civilizational bottleneck (a “Great Filter”), survival likely depends more on which paths we are going down than at what speed, except insofar as speed collapses our window to shift paths.

samuel-hammond.position: Building a unified superintelligence is a choice, not an inevitability, and is not needed for AI's benefits.
samuel-hammond.quote: We can use advanced AI to accelerate science, cure diseases, solve fusion, etc., without ever building a unified superintelligence.

samuel-hammond.position: Speeding up defensive uses of AI is the best way to help society adapt.
samuel-hammond.quote: If anything, accelerating the different modalities of defensive AI may be our best hope for making the “mitigation and adaptation” option the path of less resistance.

scott-alexander.position: Many social harms come from competitive traps in which actors must sacrifice shared values or be outcompeted, unless they can coordinate.
scott-alexander.quote: Once one agent learns how to become more competitive by sacrificing a common value, all its competitors must also sacrifice that value or be outcompeted and replaced by the less scrupulous.

scott-alexander.position: He puts the chance that AI causes human extinction at roughly one in three, with survival more likely than not.
scott-alexander.quote: I go back and forth more than I can really justify, but if you force me to give an estimate it’s probably around 33%; I think it’s very plausible that we die, but more likely that we survive (at least for a little while).
scott-alexander.work: Why I Am Not (As Much Of) A Doomer (As Some People)

scott-alexander.position: Deep uncertainty about AI's future is not a reason to assume it will turn out safe; one still has to estimate the risk.
scott-alexander.quote: If you’re can’t prove something either way, you need to take a best guess.
scott-alexander.work: MR Tries The Safe Uncertainty Fallacy

scott-alexander.position: Gradual progress through intermediate AI systems may give humans time and help to solve alignment before very dangerous AI appears.
scott-alexander.quote: I’m optimistic because I expect coherence to be a gradual process; while it’s possible AI suddenly switches from not-very-coherent to infinitely-coherent somewhere before the IQ 200 level, it seems at least as likely that it won’t.
scott-alexander.work: Why I Am Not (As Much Of) A Doomer (As Some People)

scott-alexander.position: Giving up advanced AI entirely would also carry serious risks of catastrophe or decline for civilization.
scott-alexander.quote: But if we don’t get AI, I think there’s a 50%+ chance in the next 100 years we end up dead or careening towards Venezuela.
scott-alexander.work: Pause For Thought: The AI Pause Debate

scott-alexander.position: Causes should be chosen by careful analysis of what helps most, not by what is currently in the news.
scott-alexander.quote: I think the common skill is trying to analyze what causes are important logically.
scott-alexander.work: In Continued Defense Of Effective Altruism

timnit-gebru.position: The push to build AGI is shaped by a bundle of ideologies she traces back to the eugenics movement.
timnit-gebru.quote: Disturbingly, we trace this goal back to the Anglo-American eugenics movement, via transhumanism.
timnit-gebru.work: The TESCREAL bundle: Eugenics and the promise of utopia through artificial general intelligence

timnit-gebru.position: Current AI systems depend on large numbers of low-paid, closely surveilled workers.
timnit-gebru.quote: The “AI” industry runs on the backs of these low-wage workers, who are kept in precarious positions
timnit-gebru.work: The Exploited Labor Behind Artificial Intelligence

timnit-gebru.position: Supporting worker organizing across countries should be central to ethical AI.
timnit-gebru.quote: Supporting transnational worker organizing should be at the center of the fight for “ethical AI.”
timnit-gebru.work: The Exploited Labor Behind Artificial Intelligence

timnit-gebru.position: Labor protections and antitrust measures are the first safeguards against unsafe uses of AI.
timnit-gebru.quote: When people ask what regulations need to be in place to safeguard us from the unsafe uses of AI we’ve been seeing, I always start with labor protections and antitrust measures.
timnit-gebru.work: For truly ethical AI, its research must be independent from big tech

timnit-gebru.position: Public funding should support AI research independent of large technology companies.
timnit-gebru.quote: We need an independent source of government funding to nourish independent AI research institutes that can be alternatives to the hugely concentrated power of a few large tech companies and the elite universities closely intertwined with them.
timnit-gebru.work: For truly ethical AI, its research must be independent from big tech

timnit-gebru.position: Safe AI systems should be well-scoped and built for specific tasks and communities.
timnit-gebru.quote: Building safe systems requires us to envision them as well-scoped and constrained rather than what AGI is billed to be.
timnit-gebru.work: The TESCREAL bundle: Eugenics and the promise of utopia through artificial general intelligence

tyler-cowen.position: AI is a transformational advance whose benefits will considerably outweigh its disruptions.
tyler-cowen.quote: In my view the good will considerably outweigh the bad (at least from losing #2, not #1), but I do understand that the absolute quantity of the bad disruptions will be high.
tyler-cowen.work: Existential risk, AI, and the inevitable turn in human history

tyler-cowen.position: No one can reliably predict the long-run outcomes of radical technological change.
tyler-cowen.quote: No one is good at predicting the longer-term or even medium-term outcomes of these radical technological changes (we can do the short term, albeit imperfectly).
tyler-cowen.work: Existential risk, AI, and the inevitable turn in human history

tyler-cowen.position: Human and institutional bottlenecks will make AI's boost to economic growth gradual.
tyler-cowen.quote: I’ve gone on record as suggesting that AI will boost economic growth rates by half a percentage point a year.
tyler-cowen.work: Why I think AI take-off is relatively slow

tyler-cowen.position: Society should proceed with AI development rather than halt it.
tyler-cowen.quote: So we should take the plunge.
tyler-cowen.work: Existential risk, AI, and the inevitable turn in human history

tyler-cowen.position: Alignment work is worthwhile, as ordinary improvement of a technology.
tyler-cowen.quote: Nonetheless I am still for people doing constructive work on the problem of alignment, just as we do with all other technologies, to improve them.
tyler-cowen.work: Existential risk, AI, and the inevitable turn in human history

venkatesh-rao.position: Fears of superintelligent AI rest on poorly defined, human-like traits projected onto machines, so they are not well-posed problems.
venkatesh-rao.quote: We’re using two rhyming kinds of philosophical nonsense (one that might plausibly point to something real in our experience of ourselves, and the other something imputed, via extrapolation, to a technological system) to create a theater of fictive agency around made-up problems.

venkatesh-rao.position: Modern AI is better seen as an instrument of discovery that reveals structure in data than as an invented engine.
venkatesh-rao.quote: Modern AI has the reverse problem. It’s a camera that tricks us into thinking it’s an engine that “generates” rather than “sees” things.

venkatesh-rao.position: No single moral movement, including effective altruism, should hold a monopoly over how AI is understood and governed.
venkatesh-rao.quote: No faction should get to settle the moral meaning of AI for everyone else, or act unilaterally and pre-emptively to foreclose particular futures for all.

venkatesh-rao.position: Abundant AI may expand demand for intelligence and free people for new pursuits, as agricultural productivity once did.
venkatesh-rao.quote: It may be that most minds, human and eventually artificial, are liberated from the necessity of producing intelligence merely to survive, and become free to discover what they actually want to do with it.

venkatesh-rao.position: The pace of frontier AI should be moderated mainly through market feedback rather than administrative limits.
venkatesh-rao.quote: The objective should not be to decide administratively how fast AI is allowed to improve.
venkatesh-rao.work: The Accelerationist Case for Frontier Pacing

venkatesh-rao.position: AI should be handled through well-governed human-AI systems at real control points, not through permanent human control.
venkatesh-rao.quote: The correct opposite of uncontrolled AI is therefore not human-controlled AI but well-governed human-AI systems.

vitalik-buterin.position: Technology should be accelerated, with priority on tools that favor defense and spread power rather than concentrate it.
vitalik-buterin.quote: Build technologies that shift the offense/defense balance toward defense, and do so in a way that does not rely on handing over more power to centralized authorities.

vitalik-buterin.position: The benefits of technology have been very large, and delaying progress has high costs.
vitalik-buterin.quote: the benefits of technology are really friggin massive, on those axes where we can measure if the good massively outshines the bad, and the costs of even a decade of delay are incredibly high.

vitalik-buterin.position: Centralized control for the sake of safety has its own risks, because the center can be the source of harm.
vitalik-buterin.quote: The risk of this approach is, of course, that the center is often itself the source of risk.

vitalik-buterin.position: Strong defensive technologies, such as secure computing, can make AI takeover scenarios much less likely.
vitalik-buterin.quote: Rather, my view is that the "endgame" of cybersecurity is very defense-favoring, and with the kinds of rapid technology development that AI 2027 assumes, we can get there.

vitalik-buterin.position: A future where humans become pets of superintelligent AI should be avoided; human agency should be preserved.
vitalik-buterin.quote: The goal is to build a world where we preserve human agency, achieving both the negative freedom of avoiding active interference (whether from other people acting as private citizens, or from governments, or from superintelligent bots) with our ability to shape our own destinies

vitalik-buterin.position: Broad coalitions across different fields are needed to offer an alternative to domination, deceleration and doom.
vitalik-buterin.quote: If we want to create a brighter alternative to domination, deceleration and doom, we need this kind of broad coalition building.

william-macaskill.position: AI that can do research could compress a century of technological progress into a few years.
william-macaskill.quote: AI that can accelerate research could drive a century of technological progress over just a few years.

william-macaskill.position: Making a good future even better deserves roughly as much priority as avoiding catastrophe.
william-macaskill.quote: This essay series will argue that work on Flourishing is in the same ballpark of priority as work on Surviving.

william-macaskill.position: Society should aim for a state that keeps options open and supports reflective choices, not a fixed utopian end-state.
william-macaskill.quote: From my point of view, the key priority in the world today is to get us closer to viatopia, not to some particular narrow end-state.

william-macaskill.position: Deciding what character AI systems have, and getting companies to build them that way, is among the most valuable work today.
william-macaskill.quote: We think that figuring out what characters AI systems should have, and getting companies to actually build them that way, is among the most valuable things that people can do today.

william-macaskill.position: Effective altruism should widen its focus to making the transition to a post-AGI society go well.
william-macaskill.quote: EA should embrace the mission of making the transition to a post-AGI society go well, significantly expanding our cause area focus beyond traditional AI safety.
william-macaskill.work: Effective altruism in the age of AGI

william-macaskill.position: Human institutions and decision-making cannot keep pace with AI-driven technological change.
william-macaskill.quote: But the crucial thing is that human reasoning, human decision making, and human institutions don’t speed up to match the pace of technological development.
william-macaskill.work: Will MacAskill on AI causing a 'century in a decade' and how we're completely unprepared

yann-lecun.position: Large language models are useful but are not a path to human-level intelligence.
yann-lecun.quote: They're useful, there's no question. But they are not a path towards human-level intelligence.
yann-lecun.work: Meta's AI Chief Yann LeCun on AGI, Open-Source, and AI Risk

yann-lecun.position: Human-level AI requires systems that learn world models from perception, not just text.
yann-lecun.quote: The vast majority of human knowledge is not expressed in text. It’s in the subconscious part of your mind, that you learned in the first year of life before you could speak.
yann-lecun.work: Meta's AI Chief Yann LeCun on AGI, Open-Source, and AI Risk

yann-lecun.position: AI platforms should be open source so that diverse cultures and democracies are served.
yann-lecun.quote: So the future has to be open source, if nothing else, for reasons of cultural diversity, democracy, diversity.
yann-lecun.work: Meta's AI Chief Yann LeCun on AGI, Open-Source, and AI Risk

yann-lecun.position: Intelligence does not bring a drive to dominate, so smart AI need not seek control.
yann-lecun.quote: The desire to dominate is not correlated with intelligence at all.
yann-lecun.work: Meta's AI Chief Yann LeCun on AGI, Open-Source, and AI Risk

yann-lecun.position: AI is made safe by building objectives and guardrails into its design.
yann-lecun.quote: Putting drives into AI systems is the only way to make them controllable and safe. I call this objective-driven AI.
yann-lecun.work: How Not to Be Stupid About AI, With Yann LeCun

yann-lecun.position: Misuse is best countered by widely shared, faster-advancing AI held by well-intentioned actors.
yann-lecun.quote: Then it’s my good AI against your bad AI. The way to stay ahead is to progress faster. The way to progress faster is to open the research, so the larger community contributes to it.
yann-lecun.work: How Not to Be Stupid About AI, With Yann LeCun

yoshua-bengio.position: Growing autonomy and agency in AI systems is the most worrying trend in AI today.
yoshua-bengio.quote: But what I’m most worried about today is increasing agency of AI.
yoshua-bengio.work: The Catastrophic Risks of AI — and a Safer Path (transcript)

yoshua-bengio.position: The safest AI would have no agency and only provide scientific understanding of the world.
yoshua-bengio.quote: the safest kind of AI I can imagine is one with no agency at all, only a scientific understanding of the world (which could already be immensely useful).

yoshua-bengio.position: No single person, corporation or government should be able to abuse the power of advanced AI.
yoshua-bengio.quote: We need to make sure that no single human, no single corporation and no single government can abuse the power of AGI at the expense of the common good.
yoshua-bengio.work: Reasoning through arguments against taking AI safety seriously

yoshua-bengio.position: International AI treaties need shared interest and verifiable compliance to succeed.
yoshua-bengio.quote: Two of conditions for success are (a) a common interest in the treaty (here, avoiding humanity's extinction) and (b) compliance verifiability.
yoshua-bengio.work: Reasoning through arguments against taking AI safety seriously

yoshua-bengio.position: The benefits of advanced AI must be shared globally and AI must not become a tool of domination.
yoshua-bengio.quote: such a treaty must include that AI is not used as a domination tool, including economically, and that its scientific, technological and economic benefits must be shared globally.
yoshua-bengio.work: Reasoning through arguments against taking AI safety seriously

yoshua-bengio.position: Uncertainty about when AGI arrives is a reason for urgency, not delay.
yoshua-bengio.quote: And the uncertainty in timeline means that, yes, there is urgency in doing these things, in case AGI happens faster than expected.
yoshua-bengio.work: Reasoning through arguments against taking AI safety seriously

zvi-mowshowitz.position: Most sincere disagreements about AI come down to different expectations about future AI capabilities.
zvi-mowshowitz.quote: Sincere disagreements about AI are usually disagreements about future AI capabilities.

zvi-mowshowitz.position: AI is likely to do approximately everything better than humans within our lifetimes.
zvi-mowshowitz.quote: ASI pilled. AI will be able to do approximately all the things better than you, within our natural lifetimes.

zvi-mowshowitz.position: Superintelligence should not be built until the risks of human extinction and loss of control are very low.
zvi-mowshowitz.quote: We should not build superintelligence until such time as that changes, and the risk of everyone dying as a result, as well as the risk of losing control over the future as a result, is very low.
zvi-mowshowitz.work: New Statement Calls For Not Building Superintelligence For Now

zvi-mowshowitz.position: Iterative deployment works only if it is used to fix underlying alignment problems, not to patch symptoms one at a time.
zvi-mowshowitz.quote: If you use iterative development to spot the underlying problem, it can work. If you use iterative development to patch the marginal issue over and over, then you are sitting on a time bomb.

zvi-mowshowitz.position: Much more investment in alignment, oversight, transparency, safety testing and auditing is low-cost and clearly justified now.
zvi-mowshowitz.quote: There is no good case for not doing radically more investment in alignment, infrastructure and oversight, state capacity, transparency, liability, disclosures, safety testing including of internal models, red teaming, auditing, enforcement of export controls

zvi-mowshowitz.position: Limiting the training of more powerful models is the most workable point at which to limit AI capabilities.
zvi-mowshowitz.quote: The training of more powerful models is also by far the most promising bottleneck, in the long term, through which to limit AI capabilities to ones we can handle
zvi-mowshowitz.work: On the FLI AI-Risk Open Letter
